exploration.title: Heat House
exploration.subject: Physics
exploration.summary: Change wall insulation, material and window area while comparing heat loss at matched temperatures.
exploration.question: Why does adding wall insulation not stop heat loss through the windows?
exploration.explanation: Thermal energy transfers from warmer places to cooler places. Insulation slows that transfer; it does not produce heat. This model holds the indoor and outdoor temperatures steady and calculates transfer through a fixed area of walls and windows. Adding windows replaces some opaque wall rather than enlarging the house. It omits the roof, floor, drafts, sunlight and stored heat. Material values describe a teaching example, not a real home or an energy-bill estimate.

experiments.title: Add wall insulation
experiments.instruction: Choose Add wall insulation. Will adding wall insulation reduce the heat transfer through unchanged windows? Select your prediction, then Set baseline and Add 10 cm insulation. Keep brick walls, 8 m² of windows, 20°C inside and 0°C outside. Compare no added insulation with 10 cm. Both temperatures are held steady.
experiments.observe: Wall transfer falls from 2066 W to 346 W. Window transfer stays 448 W. Combined transfer falls from 2514 W to 794 W. Why does extra wall insulation reduce only one heat-transfer path in this comparison? What else would need to change to reduce the window transfer?

experiments.title: Change window area
experiments.instruction: Choose Change window area. With insulated walls, what happens to heat loss if windows replace more of the wall area? Select your prediction, then Set baseline and Use 18 m² windows. Keep 10 cm of added insulation, brick, 20°C inside and 0°C outside. Increase windows from 2 to 18 m² within the same 60 m² wall envelope.
experiments.observe: Opaque wall area falls from 58 to 42 m². Combined transfer rises from 498 W to 1288 W because these windows transfer more heat per square meter than these insulated walls. Why must window area replace wall area for a fair comparison? Would every real window and wall have this same result?

exploration.misconception: Insulation does not generate warmth or stop all heat transfer. It slows transfer through the part of the building where it is installed.
